SolaREIT has surpassed $8.5 billion in project value supported through its real estate financing, covering approximately 4.6 gigawatts of solar and battery storage capacity.

candidates.text:
SolaREIT Supports Over $8.5 Billion In Clean Energy Project Value
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 12:56 PM
SolaREIT Supports Over $8.5 Billion In Clean Energy Project Value
SolaREIT has surpassed $8.5 billion in project value supported through its real estate financing, covering approximately 4.6 gigawatts of solar and battery storage capacity.
The milestone represents more than $3.5 billion in additional project value since November 2025. It measures the value of associated energy projects rather than the amount of financing directly provided by SolaREIT.
The Virginia-based company offers land purchases, lease purchases and land loans across all 50 states.
Its services cover utility-scale and distributed solar, battery energy storage and related infrastructure, including substation and transmission land.
The model allows developers and project owners to access capital tied to project real estate. Management said that flexibility is important when financing conditions, procurement plans and interconnection schedules change.
Co-Founder and CEO Laura Pagliarulo described land as an asset developers can use to raise capital in a constrained funding environment.
Chief Financial Officer and Chief Operating Officer Laura Klein said transactions can close within 30 to 45 days of signing, using diligence built around information developers already hold about their projects.
Founded in 2020 as a real estate investment trust, SolaREIT is a woman-owned and led business established by clean energy industry executives.
Its team brings experience across project development, finance, real estate and community solar. The company works with both developers and landowners.
The milestone reflects growth in real estate financing as one component of renewable energy project funding.
SolaREIT’s offering focuses specifically on land, providing developers with an additional source of capital alongside the other financing needed to build and operate solar, storage and associated infrastructure.
The company said its team’s industry experience helps it evaluate complex transactions and structure financing around project timelines.
KEY QUOTES:
“We pride ourselves on being a trusted partner to developers and project owners, helping them create additional value in a capital-constrained environment. It’s been another turbulent year, with higher interest rates and shifting policy, and the land under their projects is one of the few assets developers can turn into capital quickly. Surpassing $8.5 billion in project value financed reflects the trust our partners place in us. Our team has over 300 years of collective experience in the clean energy space, which allows us to help developers finance even their most complex deals.”
Laura Pagliarulo, Co-Founder And CEO Of SolaREIT
“In this market, speed and flexibility matter. With interconnection deadlines and procurement plans constantly shifting, developers need capital solutions that work on their timeline. We build our diligence on what developers already know about their projects, so we can close in 30 to 45 days from signing, providing developers with capital on a schedule they can plan around.”
Laura Klein, Chief Financial Officer And Chief Operating Officer Of SolaREIT

candidates.snippet:
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust has agreed to acquire a 75% majority interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services in a transaction valued at approximately $5 billion.
The post Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion AWS Data Center Transaction appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
candidates.text:
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion AWS Data Center Transaction
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 1:04 PM
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Announces $5 Billion AWS Data Center Transaction
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust has agreed to acquire a 75% majority interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services in a transaction valued at approximately $5 billion.
The acquisition represents the recently listed company’s first investment and carries an initial capitalization rate of 7%. The joint ventures will own 13 newly constructed powered shells across two AWS data center campuses.
AWS will retain a 25% interest in the ventures and lease the entire portfolio on a triple-net basis. The initial lease term is 12 years, with extensions potentially taking the total term to 32 years.
The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to closing conditions.
The investment establishes a starting portfolio aligned with the trust’s strategy of acquiring stabilized data centers leased to major cloud providers under long-term contracts.
CEO and President Nick Pell identified asset quality, pricing and the tenant relationship as reasons for deploying proceeds from the company’s initial public offering into the portfolio.
For AWS, the arrangement combines continued occupancy with minority ownership. The company said the partnership supports its expansion while maintaining its focus on local employment, workforce training and community priorities.
Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust targets newly constructed, income-generating facilities leased to investment-grade hyperscale tenants. Its strategy emphasizes contractual cash flows, rent increases and further acquisitions.
The company is externally managed by a Blackstone affiliate. Blackstone manages nearly $1.4 trillion across real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure and other strategies.
Morgan Stanley, CBRE Capital Markets, Citi, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan and Wells Fargo are serving as financial advisors on the transaction. Simpson Thacher & Bartlett is advising Blackstone legally.
KEY QUOTES
“We are thrilled to announce BXDC’s inaugural investment and our partnership with Amazon, a leading global technology company with a long-term commitment to innovation. The quality, basis and tenant profile of these assets make this an attractive match for the deployment of our IPO proceeds. Given the deep expertise across our platform, we believe BXDC is well positioned to capitalize on a highly compelling opportunity and deliver value for our shareholders.”
Nick Pell, CEO And President Of Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust
“As we scale to meet growing demand for our customers, we’re committed to building in a way that strengthens the communities where we operate. We’re focused on delivering long-term local benefits, from creating good jobs and free workforce training programs to supporting local priorities. Partnering with Blackstone allows us to continue expanding responsibly while keeping communities at the center of how we build.”
Prasad Kalyanaraman, Vice President Of AWS Infrastructure

Plural Raises USD 1.1 Billion to Invest in Europe's AI, Robotics and Defense Startups
Plural, a UK venture firm, raised EUR 1 billion (USD 1.10 billion) for its third fund. Two-thirds goes to early-stage startups, and the rest backs current portfolio companies. It targets energy, AI infrastructure, defense and healthcare. Six tech founders and executives lead the firm.
Written By:
Murali Teja
Reviewed By:
Manisha Sharma
Published on :
16 Nov 2026, 12:35 pm
Updated on :
16 Nov 2026, 12:35 pm
Copied
UK-based venture capital firm Plural has raised EUR 1 billion (USD 1.10 billion) for its third fund. The money will back technology startups across Europe. The firm plans to focus on energy, AI infrastructure, defense and healthcare.
The new fund shows that investors are paying more attention to European tech. Many of them want companies that build tools for key industries.
Pural Sets its Investment Priorities
Plural will put two-thirds of the fund into early-stage startups. The rest will go to companies it already backs. This extra money will help them grow.
The firm wants to find startups that can become large businesses. Its list of interests is wide. It includes AI infrastructure, chip making, the factories that produce chips, robotics and defense technology.
The firm does not plan to bet on just one area. It wants to back founders who know their field well and who want to build companies that compete around the world.
Six Partners Lead Plural's Investment Strategy
A group of tech founders and business leaders started Plural in 2022. Since then, it has invested in several European companies . These include Helsing, Proxima Fusion, OLIX and The Exploration Company.
Six partners lead the firm. They are Taavet Hinrikus, who co-founded Wise, and Sten Tamkivi, who co-founded Teleport. Ian Hogarth, who co-founded Songkick, is also a partner. So is Khaled Helioui, a former chief executive of Bigpoint. Carina Namih, who co-founded HelixNano, and Pierre-Dimitri Gore-Coty, a former Uber executive, complete the team.
Hinrikus said the firm has no fixed view on which sector will produce the next big company. Instead, the partners want to work with founders who have deep knowledge of their own industries.

A Boost for Europe's Strategic Technology Ambitions
The new fund adds fresh money to Europe's startup scene. Its focus on energy, chips, robotics and defense also fits a wider need. Europe wants stronger industry and more control over key technology.
For founders, the news means more support is available as they try to grow. For Plural, it means more room to back new ideas and to stand by the companies already in its portfolio.

candidates.text:
Sofinnova Partners: $815 Million Crossover II Fund Closes To Back Late-Stage Life Sciences Companies
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:29 AM
Sofinnova Partners: $815 Million Crossover II Fund Closes To Back Late-Stage Life Sciences Companies
Sofinnova Partners, a European life sciences venture capital firm, has completed the final close of Sofinnova Crossover II at €725 million, equivalent to approximately $815 million. The fund exceeded its original fundraising target and will invest primarily in European clinical-stage biotechnology and medical technology companies preparing for later-stage development, global expansion, and commercialization.
The new vehicle is expected to support approximately 15 companies over its investment period.
While its primary focus will be Europe, the fund will also pursue selected opportunities in the United States and other international markets.
Sofinnova believes the successful fundraising reflects increasing investor confidence in European life sciences businesses developing technologies with global commercial potential.
The fund will provide capital to companies approaching important stages of clinical development and business growth.
Supporting Clinical Development And Commercialization
Life sciences companies frequently require substantial financing to advance experimental therapies and medical technologies through clinical testing, regulatory approval, and commercialization.
Sofinnova Crossover II is designed to support businesses during these later stages of development.
Its investment strategy focuses on companies with promising scientific foundations, clinical validation, and leadership teams capable of expanding internationally.
Sofinnova believes the European market is producing an increasing number of competitive healthcare companies that need access to substantial growth capital.
The firm’s investment approach combines financial backing with industry expertise and strategic support.
Building On Crossover I
Sofinnova’s first crossover fund invested in several companies that subsequently completed significant corporate transactions or public market milestones.
These include LimFlow, acquired by Inari Medical; Calliditas Therapeutics, acquired by Asahi Kasei; and Amolyt Pharma, acquired by AstraZeneca.
The portfolio also included Abivax, which achieved a Nasdaq listing.
These investments demonstrate the firm’s strategy of backing life sciences companies as they advance toward larger commercial markets.
Crossover II has already invested in Hemab Therapeutics, CellCentric, and Neurent Medical.
The fund will continue seeking opportunities among biotechnology and medical technology companies with differentiated products and clinical development programs.
Investment Leadership And Institutional Support
The Crossover II strategy is led by Sofinnova partners Joe Anderson, Kinam Hong, Cedric Moreau, Jacques Theurillat, and David Evans.
The fund is supported by the European Tech Champions Initiative, a fund-of-funds managed by the European Investment Fund.
Sofinnova Partners was founded in 1972 and operates from Paris, London, and Milan.
The firm has invested in more than 500 companies across its history and currently manages more than €4 billion in assets.
Its investment activities span life sciences and sustainability, from early-stage company formation through later-stage development.
The new €725 million fund strengthens Sofinnova’s capacity to support European life sciences companies seeking to compete internationally.
KEY QUOTES:
“The scale of this fund reflects both the maturity of the European life sciences ecosystem and the rising demand for capital that can help companies to reach global markets. Europe is producing a growing number of world-class life sciences companies, and we believe they should have access to investors that can support them through the critical stages of growth and commercialization.”
Antoine Papiernik, Chairman And Managing Partner Of Sofinnova Partners
“We continue to see exceptional opportunities emerging across European life sciences. Many companies now have scientific strength, clinical validation, and leadership teams needed to compete on a global stage. With Sofinnova Crossover II, we are well positioned to support that next generation of leaders while maintaining the disciplined investment approach that defined our first fund.”
Kinam Hong, Partner At Sofinnova Partners

JBS Announces $542 Million Flora Acquisition To Enter Personal Care Market
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:20 PM
JBS Announces $542 Million Flora Acquisition To Enter Personal Care Market
JBS has agreed to acquire Brazilian consumer products company Flora for $542 million, expanding into beauty and personal care while adding to its household cleaning business.
Flora is owned by J&F Group, JBS’s controlling shareholder. The transaction therefore brings a business from its controlling shareholder into the company.
The purchase includes assumed debt, with $367 million in equity consideration payable entirely through JBS treasury Class A shares, Brazilian depositary receipts or a combination of both.
JBS expects no change to its net leverage ratio based on Flora’s earnings contribution and the transaction structure.
Flora generated R$2.9 billion, approximately $531 million, in annual net revenue for the 12 months ended September 2026. Its brands include Minuano, Francis, Neutrox and OX.
The company operates five factories, seven distribution centers and a research and development center, employing more than 4,200 people.
Flora originated as JBS’s hygiene and cleaning division before separating in 2007. The businesses have maintained commercial ties, including JBS’s supply of beef tallow for cleaning and hygiene products.
JBS intends to connect its ingredients and collagen capabilities with Flora’s brands, distribution and consumer products expertise.
The acquisition complements Genu-in, established in 2022 to develop collagen applications, and research activities at JBS Biotech and BioTech Foods.
JBS also announced an $11 million acquisition of Canal Rural, an agribusiness-focused Brazilian media company, on a cash-free, debt-free basis. The final price will be adjusted for closing net debt.
Both acquisitions are expected to close in December 2026, subject to customary conditions.
The transactions broaden JBS’s activities beyond its global food portfolio, with Flora providing an established platform for expansion into adjacent consumer categories.

candidates.title: Agile Robots raises $500 million led by SoftBank
candidates.snippet: Agile Robots raises $500 million led by SoftBank CASRAI
candidates.text:
Munich-based Agile Robots announced on November 12, 2026 that it had closed a $500 million Series F led by SoftBank Group, with NVIDIA among the participants. The financing supports international expansion and manufacturing, putting fresh capital behind a robotics business whose research connections include Franka Robotics and a Google DeepMind partnership. Reuters confirmed the announcement .
A $500 million round for expansion and production
The round values Agile Robots at $8.5 billion and takes its total funding to $2 billion. Alongside SoftBank and NVIDIA, participants include Hitachi Group, comprising Hitachi and Hitachi Ventures, and T.Capital. The company’s November 12 announcement says the proceeds will support a larger presence in the United States, additional production capacity including in Germany, and entry into new markets.
Founder and chief executive Zhaopeng Chen described the financing as a way to accelerate expansion and bring intelligent robots into industrial production. SoftBank Investment Advisers managing partner Dennis Chang said Agile combines robotics expertise with industrial execution, adding: “We believe Physical AI will transform industries.” These are the company’s and investor’s expectations for the business.
Tech.eu’s November 12 report places the investment in an existing industrial operation: Agile’s machines assemble products, handle components, inspect equipment and move materials through factories. Its portfolio extends across robotic arms, hands, autonomous mobile robots and humanoids, together with their software and AI models.
Factory capacity and installed systems measure different things
Reuters reported that Agile opened its Fürstenfeldbruck factory, near Munich, earlier in 2026. The company says it can produce up to 10,000 legged and wheeled humanoid robots annually. That is a stated capacity ceiling, rather than a report of annual output or shipments.
Separately, Agile reports more than 20,000 robotic solutions installed worldwide. Its announcement describes deployments across automotive, consumer electronics, logistics and other industries; it does not identify that total as humanoid installations. Treating the two numbers as interchangeable would obscure the difference between the company’s established industrial business and its humanoid manufacturing ambitions.
The financing release also gives no allocation of the proceeds between the United States, German production and other markets. It therefore establishes the expansion priorities without quantifying how much additional capacity each location will receive.
A research spin-off with an academic hardware connection
Agile was founded in 2018 as a spin-off from the German Aerospace Center, according to Reuters and Tech.eu. The company reports more than 2,000 research and development specialists and over 650 patents. Its path from a public research institution into industrial automation provides a concrete technology transfer connection for universities following the investment.
There is also a direct research equipment link. Franka Robotics says it has belonged to Agile Robots since 2023. Franka describes its Research 3 system as a force-sensitive platform for robotics and AI, giving researchers low-level access to robot control and learning capabilities. Its website also says Agile’s Diana 7 now supports the Franka Control Interface, extending the ecosystem to a robot with greater reach and payload capacity.
The funding follows earlier DeepMind and NVIDIA announcements
The Series F is a financing development alongside earlier technical collaborations. On March 24, Agile announced a research partnership with Google DeepMind to combine Gemini Robotics foundation models with its hardware. The partners described an initial focus on industrial and manufacturing tasks, using deployment, data collection, training and iteration to improve their systems.
In that announcement, DeepMind robotics head Carolina Parada presented the collaboration as a step toward bringing AI into real-world applications across sectors. The research mechanism matters: operational robot data is intended to inform model development, rather than the partnership consisting only of installing a fixed model on a machine.
A separate Agile release published October 27 says NVIDIA announced plans to invest on October 19. It dates the introduction of the Agile ONE SN research humanoid at NVIDIA GTC Berlin to October 21. Those October events provide background to NVIDIA’s participation in the November round.
What this means for universities and research offices
For robotics laboratories, the connection is unusually specific: the funded group includes a research arm platform and is developing a humanoid reference platform. Agile says ONE SN uses NVIDIA’s Isaac GR00T development platform and Jetson Thor computing. Its October release also describes Diana arms supporting the Franka Control Interface, linking the company’s industrial portfolio to an interface already offered for research.
For research offices, the practical distinction is between investment, equipment access and collaboration terms. The March partnership explicitly involves operational data and model iteration. That makes data use and project outputs relevant subjects for a research collaboration agreement ; the Series F announcement itself does not supply those terms or announce university grants. This is an implication of the described research workflow, rather than a new funding opportunity for institutions.
The next stated milestone is early 2027
Agile’s October release places planned ONE SN availability in early 2027. It also describes a pilot involving Agile, Audi, Dassault Systèmes and NVIDIA at Audi’s Ingolstadt plant, where mobile humanoids pick and sequence parts. The company describes testing the workcell in a virtual twin before physical deployment.
These are distinct stages of development: a planned research platform, an industrial pilot and manufacturing

candidates.text:
VICI Properties: $500 Million Unsecured Term Loan Refinances 2027 Debt And Improves Revolving Credit Facility Pricing
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 5:35 PM
VICI Properties: $500 Million Unsecured Term Loan Refinances 2027 Debt And Improves Revolving Credit Facility Pricing
VICI Properties, a real estate investment trust specializing in gaming, hospitality, entertainment, and experiential properties, has secured a new $500 million unsecured term loan through its subsidiary VICI Properties L.P. The financing will be used to partially refinance the company’s outstanding senior unsecured notes maturing in February 2027, while an accompanying amendment reduces borrowing costs under its existing $2.5 billion revolving credit facility.
The new loan matures on January 31, 2032, extending a portion of VICI’s debt maturity profile by approximately five years.
The loan initially carries an interest rate of the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) plus 90 basis points, based on a pricing grid tied to the subsidiary’s credit ratings.
The agreement also includes an improvement in pricing when the company’s total leverage ratio is at or below a specified threshold.
VICI drew the entire $500 million at closing and entered into swap agreements covering the full principal amount.
These arrangements establish an effective all-in fixed interest rate of approximately 5.20%.
The financing will help VICI address a meaningful portion of its February 2027 debt maturity by partially redeeming and refinancing its 5.75% senior unsecured notes.
By replacing part of the approaching maturity with longer-dated financing, VICI is seeking to improve its debt maturity schedule and maintain financial flexibility.
The transaction also diversifies the company’s available funding sources.
Alongside the term loan, VICI amended its existing $2.5 billion unsecured revolving credit facility.
The amendment lowers the applicable interest rate from SOFR plus 85 basis points to SOFR plus 80 basis points, subject to the company’s ratings-based pricing grid and leverage-related adjustments.
The revolving facility’s borrowing capacity and maturity remain unchanged.
These changes provide VICI with improved pricing on a significant source of corporate liquidity.
Wells Fargo Securities served as sole bookrunner for the term loan, while Wells Fargo Bank acted as administrative agent.
Wells Fargo Securities, Mizuho Bank, Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, and Truist Securities served as joint lead arrangers.
Additional participating financial institutions included Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase Bank, Capital One, Citizens Bank, Scotiabank, Barclays, Citibank, Goldman Sachs Bank USA, and Texas Capital Bank.
VICI Properties maintains one of the largest portfolios of experiential real estate assets in North America.
The company’s holdings include 103 experiential properties, comprising 63 gaming properties and 40 other experiential assets across the United States and Canada.
Its portfolio encompasses approximately 130 million square feet and includes more than 67,000 hotel rooms and over 700 restaurants, bars, nightclubs, and sportsbooks.
Major holdings include Caesars Palace Las Vegas, MGM Grand, and the Venetian Resort Las Vegas.
The company leases its properties to gaming, hospitality, and entertainment operators under long-term triple-net lease agreements.
VICI also maintains real estate and financing partnerships with operators across recreational and experiential sectors, including Great Wolf Resorts, Canyon Ranch, Kalahari Resorts, Club Med, Chelsea Piers, and others.
The latest refinancing supports VICI’s broader balance sheet management strategy as it continues operating and expanding its experiential real estate portfolio.
By extending debt maturities, securing a fixed borrowing rate, and lowering revolving credit facility pricing, VICI is strengthening its financial position while maintaining access to capital for future opportunities.

“We are very pleased to close this Term Loan, which diversifies our funding sources and addresses a meaningful portion of our February 2027 maturity at an attractive fixed cost and extends our debt maturity profile. We greatly appreciate the continued support and confidence of our bank group, and the improved pricing on our Revolving Credit Facility reflects the strength of our investment grade balance sheet.”
David Kieske, Executive Vice President And Chief Financial Officer Of VICI Properties

Q-CTRL, a developer of AI-powered quantum infrastructure software, has raised $290 million (A$415 million) in Series C funding led by Salesforce Ventures, with significant participation from Bullhound Capital and Affinity Partners. By Amit Chowdhry

Windward Bio Raises $225 Million In Nasdaq Debut At $1.69 Billion Market Capitalization
Windward Bio Group has completed its public market debut after pricing an initial public offering at $17 per share and raising $225 million in gross proceeds, including a $50 million concurrent private placement from Sanofi.
The clinical-stage biotechnology company began trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market on November 13, 2026 and ended its first day with a market capitalization of approximately $1.69 billion.
Windward sold approximately 10.29 million ordinary shares in the offering.
The Basel, Switzerland-based company was founded in 2024 by serial biotechnology entrepreneur Luca Santarelli, M.D., and his team. Santarelli previously helped build VectivBio and Therachon, both of which were ultimately acquired.
Windward has raised $365 million since its formation, including a $200 million Series A in January 2025 and a $165 million crossover financing in May 2026.
Pivotal bioVenture Partners China has invested in the company through each financing round from its early formation through the public listing.
Windward is developing ultra-long-acting antibody treatments for respiratory and dermatologic diseases including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and atopic dermatitis.
Its lead program, WIN378, is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting thymic stromal lymphopoietin.
WIN378 is currently being evaluated in the Phase 2/3 POLARIS-1 asthma study and the Phase 2 SIRIUS COPD trial. The drug is being developed for twice-yearly dosing, compared with the once-every-four-weeks schedule of currently approved treatments in the category.
Windward reported positive interim Phase 2 data in September 2026 supporting twice-yearly dosing of WIN378 in asthma.
Its pipeline also includes WIN027, a clinical-stage bispecific antibody targeting TSLP and IL-13 that is currently in Phase 1 development.
Global rights outside Greater China and certain Asian markets to both programs were licensed from Chinese biopharmaceutical companies.
Windward plans to use IPO proceeds to support clinical development of WIN378 and WIN027, advance additional bispecific antibody programs and fund working capital and general corporate purposes.
The company expects top-line Phase 2 asthma data for WIN378 in the first half of 2027, Phase 2 COPD data in the second half of 2027 and Phase 3 asthma data in the first half of 2029.

Lincoln – Attorney General Mike Hilgers announced a $183.5 million multistate settlement with Acima Digital, LLC, and its parent company, Acima Holdings, LLC. Acima, a rent-to-own financing company that partners with Nebraska retailers, was accused of misleading consumers about the terms and costs of its rental-purchase agreements. Forty-three states alleged that Acima advertised 90-day payoff programs without clearly disclosing that consumers were automatically placed in 12-month agreements and could end up paying twice the advertised cash price. The company also allegedly misrepresented its services as traditional credit, marked up merchandise prices, and made it difficult for consumers to return merchandise and end agreements.
Under the settlement, Acima must improve retail partner training, provide clearer advertising and contract disclosures, stop marking up merchandise prices, allow consumers to return merchandise without obstruction, and properly address delivery, damage, and repair issues. The company also cannot report rental-purchase agreements to the three major credit bureaus for five years.
Consumers eligible for restitution or lease forgiveness do not need to take action. The settlement administrator will contact consumers receiving restitution, while Acima will notify those eligible for lease forgiveness.

BARCELONA, Spain , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stark Future, the Barcelona company behind the world's best-selling enduro motorcycle, today announced the close of a financing round with a total transaction value in excess of €150 million, the largest investment ever made in a European electric motorcycle company. The round values Stark Future at €1.2 billion pre-money, making it Europe's first electric motorcycle company valued above €1 billion. The round was led by Highland Europe, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management's 1GT climate private equity strategy and Spain-based international investment firm Axon Partners Group, with participation from existing shareholders and friends and family. The round was oversubscribed and exceeded the initial target, prompting the Company to keep the door open for a second closing to accommodate additional strategic partners, including Lombard Odier among others.

Founded in 2020 on an uncompromising belief that electric motorcycles should not just be the green alternative, but the better machine, Stark Future builds bikes designed to beat the best combustion competitors in every category they enter. Today, the VARG platform, spanning motocross, enduro and supermoto, is designed, engineered and built in-house at the Company's 20,000 m² facility on the outskirts of Barcelona. The new capital will fund global expansion and the development of new electric platforms.
In just three years of sales, Stark has gone from challenger to category leader. The VARG is now the best-selling enduro motorcycle on the planet, outselling every combustion competitor. Within its first year, Stark took around 50% of the enduro market in Germany and the top spot in France and Italy, while the United States has grown to be its largest market by volume. From a standing start, Stark has taken around 5% of the €3 billion global off-road motorcycle market from combustion in three years. The new capital is aimed at repeating that, and more, by entering new motorcycle categories, in a much larger €90 billion addressable motorcycle market. Few hardware companies grow this fast. Fewer do it profitably.
Anton Wass, Founder and CEO of Stark Future, says: "Six years ago, Stark was an unwavering belief that electric could be the better machine, not the compromise. Today it's the largest investment ever made in a European electric motorcycle company. We turned the industry on its head once with the VARG, taking 5% of a €3 billion market from combustion in three years. This gives us the resources to do it again, and more, in a €90 billion market. While others in this industry have run out of road, we've grown, turned profitable, and brought Highland Europe and world-renowned institutional investors on board, and we have kept the door open in the second closing for a few more who share the same ambition. None of it would have happened without the riders who chose a VARG before the world's biggest investors did, and the dealers who put it on their floors. Thank you for making this dream real. We're not here to take part in the future of motorcycling. We're here to lead it."
Tony Zappalà, Partner at Highland Europe, added: "Since selling its first bike just three years ago, Stark Future has become the go-to name in performance off-road motorcycling. It has built that traction in the most technical and unforgiving segment of the market. Once we met with Anton and the team, we caught the fever of the company's guiding principle: to build the best bike with no compromises. Motorbikes are the last major vehicle category to meaningfully undergo electrification. Many have tried, but no one has matched Stark's success. We believe it will be the company that leads the transition with best-in-class performance."
Vikram Raju, Head of Climate Private Equity Investing at Morgan Stanley Investment Management and 1GT, said: "The most compelling climate solutions are often those that do not ask their customers to compromise. Stark Future is a powerful example of that, combining a relentless focus on engineering excellence with electric motorcycles built to compete on performance first. At 1GT, we back ambitious founders and teams whose products and solutions have the potential to create meaningful real-world impact and advance the transition to a lower-carbon economy. We are excited to support the company's next phase of growth and look forward to bringing the resources and global capabilities of Morgan Stanley to the partnership as Stark continues to scale internationally."
Alfonso de León, Managing Partner at Axon Partners Group , said: "Stark is the rare technology and performance company that grows like a tech business and earns like an industrial one. As a Spanish-based investment firm, Axon is proud to invest alongside Highland, 1GT, and a group of world-class investors to support a Spanish company leading a global category. This is just the beginning of what Stark will become."
Stifel served as the lead financial adviser to Stark Future for this transaction. This investment brings long-term backing from major institutional investors, including Highland Europe, whose portfolio features category-leading companies such as Wolt, GetYourGuide, Huel, and Zwift, alongside Morgan Stanley Investment Management's 1GT strategy, Axon Partners Group

Zacua Ventures raises $135 million to invest in robotics, physical AI and industrial technology
November 15, 2026 by Sam Francis
Venture capital firm Zacua Ventures has closed its second investment fund at $135 million, more than doubling the size of its original $56 million fund as it expands its focus on robotics, physical AI and technologies for industrial applications.
The San Francisco-based firm says Fund II was 35 percent oversubscribed, attracting commitments from more than 30 corporate and institutional investors across over 20 countries.
Originally focused on construction technology, Zacua is broadening its investment strategy to include manufacturing, energy, mining, infrastructure and other sectors it collectively describes as the “Physical Industries”.
The firm believes these sectors offer substantial opportunities for technologies that combine robotics, artificial intelligence and software with practical industrial expertise.
Vivin Hegde, founding partner at Zacua Ventures, says: “The industries that underpin modern life are entering a forced transformation cycle. Housing is out of reach. Energy grids are under pressure. Workforces are aging out. The AI infrastructure buildout is placing even greater demands on the industries already struggling to keep pace.
“These are not isolated problems; they’re converging across the Physical Industries, a category venture capital has largely overlooked. We built Zacua in construction because we saw these challenges firsthand. Fund II takes what we learned there and applies it to the broader physical world.”
Building on construction robotics investments
Zacua has already invested in 34 early-stage companies across 11 markets, with several investments demonstrating its interest in industrial automation.
Among its portfolio companies is Gravis Robotics, an ETH Zurich spinout developing physical AI for autonomous construction equipment. The company raised $200 million in Series A funding from SoftBank earlier this year, reaching a reported valuation of $1 billion.
Another investment is Origin Robotics, whose OG1 robot autonomously finishes interior walls. The company emerged from stealth with $20 million in seed and Series A financing, with Zacua leading the latter round.
Other investments include Flexnode, which develops modular data centers, and CURA Climate, which is working on technologies to reduce emissions from cement production.
Zacua’s first exit came earlier this year when construction risk-management software company Document Crunch was acquired by Trimble.
Expanding industrial investment
Fund II’s investors include Volvo Group Venture Capital, Holcim Maqer Ventures, Hilti Venture, Trimble Ventures, Acciona, DPR Construction, Mortenson and Dubai Future District Fund.
The firm says its corporate investor network provides portfolio companies with access to industrial customers, technical expertise and opportunities to test emerging technologies in operational environments.
Juan Nieto, founding partner at Zacua Ventures, says: “Fund I proved that our model works in one of the most complex and consequential industries in the world.
“Fund II allows us to take that same playbook much further. We are not changing what we do. We are applying the same early-stage conviction, founder-first philosophy and industry network across the broader Physical Industries.”
Zacua has already begun investing from Fund II, with robotics, industrial AI and infrastructure technologies expected to remain central to its strategy.

John Egan

Adam Blake, Nick Poradek and Seth Cohen founded Mavria this spring. Photo courtesy of Mavria
The Woodlands-based Mavria , which mass-produces factory-built modular AI data centers, just emerged from stealth mode with $130 million in funding at a $1 billion valuation.
Mavria raised the money in pre-seed and seed rounds led by Paradigm, an investment firm that concentrates on early-stage startups developing “pioneer” technology. Participants in the funding rounds include AMP PBC, Critical Frontier, Dream Ventures and Liquid 2 Ventures, co-founded by former NFL quarterback Joe Montana.
The company’s inaugural product, Terrain, is a prefabricated data center designed for AI labs, cloud computing providers and data center developers. Mavria says its platform avoids ground-up construction, delivering infrastructure more quickly and at a lower cost.
Mavria tells the Wall Street Journal that the first Terrain unit is being built at a Houston-area factory. The 5-megawatt Terrain system features power distribution, direct liquid cooling, controls and server racks.
“America sets the pace at the intelligence frontier. But the race is moving from the lab into the physical world,” Adam Blake, co-founder and CEO of Mavria, wrote in a blog post .
“Intelligence needs data centers. Data centers need power. Power needs factories, equipment, supply chains, and skilled workers, but much of that infrastructure is still built one custom project at a time, on timelines measured in years.”
Blake and Mavria’s two other co-founders, Nick Poradek and Seth Cohen, most recently worked at the U.S. Department of Energy. There, they focused on reforming the nuclear power sector.
From start to finish, it can take roughly three to six years to build a data center at an estimated cost of $10 million to $37 million per megawatt. Based on those figures, a 100-megawatt data center might cost as much as $3.7 billion.
Here are brief bios of Blake, Poradek and Cohen, who co-founded Mavria in May.
Adam Blake
Blake most recently was a senior advisor to U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright. He is co-founder and former CEO of Zego, a provider of energy management technology for property managers. Zego spun out from Brightergy, a commercial solar company. Blake is founder and former CEO of Brightergy.
Nick Poradek
Poradek , chief operating officer at Mavria, was also an advisor to the U.S. energy secretary. He is founder and former CEO of Spring-based Edera Energy, co-founder of The Woodlands-based craft-ice brand Clarity Ice, and founder and former CEO of The Woodlands-based Edera Capital. Poradek sold Edera Energy, a manufacturer of oilfield equipment, to Liberty Energy, a fracking company. Wright is Liberty’s founder and former chairman and CEO.
Seth Cohen
Cohen , chief strategy officer and chief legal officer at Mavria, was head of nuclear law and policy at the Department of Energy. He is also a former NASA advisor and a former attorney at Kirkland & Ellis.
“We believe in rapidly deploying infrastructure as a product, rather than custom-building every project,” Blake said. “We’re bringing together engineering, manufacturing, supply chains and capital so that every project makes us better at delivering the next.”

Corma argues coding-focused models suit offensive security while defense needs continuous log and event analysis.
Compute capacity rather than model quality is Corma's immediate constraint on serving demand and its waitlist.
Defensive-cybersecurity company Corma announced on November 16, 2026 that it had raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation. NEA led the round, with continued participation from Sequoia Capital , Khosla Ventures and Coatue, bringing Corma’s total funding to $185 million.
Corma said the new capital would accelerate scaling of its foundation models, expand compute capacity and support selective hiring. The Series A follows its emergence from stealth on August 10, 2026 with $60 million in seed funding.
The company characterized demand from the world’s largest organizations as overwhelming and identified securing enough compute for that demand and its waitlist as one of its central challenges. Corma’s ability to expand access therefore depends on obtaining additional infrastructure as well as advancing its models.
How the Corma Workforce Operates
The company deploys those models through the Corma Workforce , a system designed to work autonomously alongside human security teams. It operates within customers’ existing security and IT stacks, including identity, cloud, endpoint, security information and event management, and firewall or intrusion-detection tools. Its work spans investigations, connecting evidence and taking action across those systems.
Employees can assign tasks through Slack or Teams, ask questions, review findings and approve actions. The design adds AI-led execution to a customer’s current operating environment while keeping human review in the workflow.
Corma reports live deployments across healthcare, finance, energy, critical infrastructure and retail, with 99% of security tasks completed autonomously and successfully, 100 times faster end-to-end completion and 95% lower cost per completed task.
One anonymized Fortune 1000 services-company CISO quoted on the product page said end-to-end response time fell 94% in a comparison with the customer’s former service provider, which the customer subsequently replaced with Corma.
Why Corma Uses Defense-Specific Models
Corma’s launch statement argues that improvements in coding and software reasoning map more directly to offensive security than to the broader defensive workload. Vulnerability research and exploit development are code-reasoning problems against bounded targets; defense instead requires continuous analysis of audit logs, events, configurations and network flows. It also involves connecting weak signals across systems and long periods while making thousands of accurate, consistent decisions each day under changing conditions.
That distinction is the basis for Corma’s focus on domain-specific foundation models. Its stated development program includes rethinking model architecture, extending context to detect faint anomaly signals, adversarial self-play and continuous learning that can establish baselines over months and years.
CEO Alon Pluda and the Corma team said the next generation of its foundation models would be shared soon, without giving a release date. The financing supports that next phase of model development and selective hiring, but the immediate scaling constraint is compute: broader deployments require enough additional capacity to serve current demand and organizations on the waitlist.

Israeli AI language model cybersecurity company Corma , today announced the completion of a $125 million Series A financing round, at a $1 billion valuation, led by NEA, alongside existing investors Sequoia Capital, Khosla Ventures. The company has now raised $185 million, having emerged from stealth just three months ago with a $60 million seed round led by Sequoia.
CEO Alon Pluda founded the company last year, after leaving Miggo Security, which he cofounded, following a dispute with his cofounders. Pluda is a graduate of the IDF Intelligence Corps’ prestigious Psagot program. He completed his service in 2022, following several years as a career officer in various technical roles at the core of Unit 8200’s technological operations. He founded Corma, which has 20 employees in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, with the aim of more effectively addressing AI-driven cyberattacks. The company achieves this by developing language models from scratch, rather than relying on existing models such as those from Anthropic, OpenAI, and DeepSeek.
Pluda explains, "General-purpose language models are effective for tasks like software development or research and they are also excellent at identifying bugs and cyber vulnerabilities, which is precisely why hackers and attackers use them so efficiently. However, they are weak when it comes to defense. Defense requires a different kind of expertise: the ability to find a 'needle in a haystack' within the complex landscape of enterprise data systems, specifically regarding code and software maintenance, such as telemetry, logs, and events."
In Pluda’s view, this is why the language models currently on the market are highly advanced in their capacity to facilitate powerful cyberattacks, yet remain insufficiently developed for the purpose of defending organizations. Fluda explains that Corma addresses this gap by developing its own language model, which is focused entirely on a single task: perimeter defense for organizations. The company also develops AI agents that are integrated into client organizations, working alongside existing cybersecurity teams.
Pluda adds, "We don’t just provide CISOs with a dashboard or software to manage. We provide AI agents that empower them, enabling them to perform their jobs orders of magnitude better."
The company trains its models with the goal of achieving "superintelligence" for defensive cybersecurity - a capability that will allow security teams to operate at the speed and scale required to counter the advancement of AI-driven cyberattacks.
The company’s annual recurring revenue (ARR) is estimated to be in the tens of millions of dollars, and its client base includes companies from the Fortune 100 and Fortune 500 lists.
"Since its initial unveiling in August, demand for the company’s models has surged among organizations ranked in the Fortune 100, Fortune 500, and Fortune Global 500. To meet this demand, the company has increased its server capacity 24-fold," the company stated.
Corma works with large organizations, including companies in the healthcare, financial services, energy and critical infrastructure, retail, and telecommunications sectors. These organizations are increasingly delegating their security tasks to Corma’s autonomous workforce, which operates using a foundational model developed by the company.

Ameresco: $125 Million Financing From Nuveen With Expansion Capacity To $225 Million Supports European Energy Infrastructure Growth
Ameresco, an energy infrastructure company specializing in reliable power and infrastructure modernization, has secured a $125 million committed financing facility with Nuveen Energy Infrastructure Credit to support its expanding operations in the United Kingdom and Europe. The five-year revolving facility includes an option to increase financing capacity by an additional $100 million, potentially providing Ameresco with access to $225 million in total capital.
The facility matures in November 2031 and will provide dedicated financing for energy infrastructure projects and working capital requirements across Ameresco’s European business.
The financing has been structured with limited recourse to Ameresco and does not affect the company’s senior secured corporate leverage ratios.
This arrangement is intended to create a more self-sustaining capital structure for European operations while preserving financial flexibility at the parent-company level.
The facility will also allow Ameresco to expand available borrowing capacity as its project pipeline and working capital requirements increase, subject to the relevant terms.
The investment comes amid substantial growth in Ameresco’s European business.
European revenue increased from $62 million in 2022 to $529 million in 2025, representing more than an eightfold increase over that period.
The region now accounts for approximately 25% of Ameresco’s total revenue.

South African fintech company Yoco has secured a US$100 million credit facility from US investment firm Victory Park Capital to expand its merchant cash advance operation.
Yoco builds tools and services to help small businesses accept card payments in-store and online, access loans, and manage their day to day activities. The startup has advanced more than ZAR6.5 billion (US$395 million) to over 40,000 merchants since 2018, working with specialist credit providers.
The company, which secured US$83 million in Series C funding back in 2021, has now secured a US$100 million credit facility from Victory Park Capital, which will allow it to scale its cash advance operations, and gain greater control over the pricing and risk of its merchant loans.
The aim is to use the transaction data generated by merchants using Yoco’s card machines and online payment tools to assess businesses that traditional lenders may struggle to evaluate, helping the company turn its payments relationship with more than 200,000 businesses into a larger cash advance operation.

Victory Park Capital brings experience in private credit and asset-backed finance to the arrangement, having invested more than US$12 billion across 260 investments since 2007. Senior partner Jason Brown, said Yoco had demonstrated a track record of supporting small and independent businesses.

candidates.text:
Seawolf Therapeutics: $100 Million Funding And Up To $1.2 Billion Sanofi Partnership To Advance DNA Medicines
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 7:32 AM
Seawolf Therapeutics: $100 Million Funding And Up To $1.2 Billion Sanofi Partnership To Advance DNA Medicines
Seawolf Therapeutics, a San Diego-based biotechnology company developing DNA-based medicines, has emerged from stealth with $100 million in funding and announced a multi-target research collaboration with Sanofi worth up to $1.2 billion in potential milestone payments, plus royalties. The company is developing a lipid nanoparticle-based DNA delivery platform designed to enable sustained production of therapeutic proteins inside patients’ cells.
Seawolf’s financing includes seed and Series A investments backed by Versant Ventures, MPM BioImpact, Novartis Venture Fund, Eli Lilly, CRISPR Therapeutics, Sixty Degree Capital, Alexandria Venture Investments, and Pathway to Cures, the philanthropic venture arm of the National Bleeding Disorders Foundation.
Versant Ventures led the seed financing, while the Series A included Versant, MPM BioImpact, and Novartis Venture Fund.
The capital will support advancement of Seawolf’s proprietary therapeutic pipeline, including a lead program targeting metabolic diseases.
Developing The TRIDENT DNA Delivery Platform
Seawolf’s technology platform, called TRIDENT, stands for Targeted RNA-Induced DNA Expression via Nuclear Translocation.
The system uses lipid nanoparticles to transport DNA into cells and facilitate access to the nucleus, where genetic information can support production of therapeutic proteins.
Lipid nanoparticles are also used in certain RNA-based medicines, but RNA therapies can face limitations involving how long protein expression lasts.
Seawolf is developing a different approach intended to provide more durable protein production by delivering DNA-based payloads.
TRIDENT combines a proprietary lipid nanoparticle, DNA encoding a therapeutic protein, and an auxiliary factor that helps facilitate nuclear entry.
The company says its technology has demonstrated sustained protein expression above therapeutic levels in nonhuman primate studies at doses reported to be safe and well tolerated.
The company has also generated preclinical proof-of-concept results in animal models involving metabolic and rare diseases.
These findings remain preclinical and will require further evaluation before therapeutic benefits and safety can be established in humans.
A Redosable Approach To DNA Medicines
Seawolf is designing its technology to allow repeat administration when necessary.
The company describes TRIDENT as a nonviral DNA delivery approach that avoids some of the limitations associated with virus-based genetic medicine platforms.
Its goal is to provide durable protein expression while preserving the ability to adjust or supplement dosing.
The technology could support several therapeutic approaches, including replacement of defective genes and systemic production of biologic medicines.
Seawolf believes this flexibility may allow the platform to address multiple disease categories.
Sanofi Collaboration Includes Up To $1.2 Billion In Milestones
Alongside its funding announcement, Seawolf disclosed a multi-target research collaboration and exclusive license agreement with Sanofi.
The partnership will focus on developing undisclosed therapies for bleeding disorders and additional indications.
The agreement includes up to $1.2 billion in research, development, and commercialization milestone payments, along with tiered royalties on sales of any resulting products.
The milestone total represents potential future consideration contingent on the progress of the collaboration, rather than funding already received.
The agreement provides Seawolf with a major pharmaceutical partner as it advances its delivery technology.
Supporting The Next Stage Of Development
Seawolf President and CEO Elizabeth Alcamo said the funding and Sanofi partnership position the company to advance its lead program in metabolic diseases while developing therapies addressing additional unmet medical needs.
Versant Managing Director Tom Woiwode, who chairs Seawolf’s board, highlighted the potential of DNA delivery to support long-lasting production of therapeutic proteins.
With $100 million in funding and a pharmaceutical collaboration carrying substantial potential milestones, Seawolf is preparing to move its DNA delivery platform toward further therapeutic development.
KEY QUOTES
“Seawolf is charting a new course in patient care through LNP-based DNA medicines. With a strong syndicate of investors and our collaboration with Sanofi, we are well-positioned to execute on our next stage of growth, which will include advancing our lead program for metabolic diseases and collaborating with Sanofi in its mission to develop therapies for patient unmet needs.”
Dr. Elizabeth Alcamo, President And CEO Of Seawolf Therapeutics
“Nucleic acid-based therapies have advanced dramatically over the past decade. The Seawolf team is now delivering on the promise of using DNA to drive robust and long-term expression of therapeutic proteins directly from the patient’s own cells. I look forward to seeing this groundbreaking technology transform treatment options for patients.”
Dr. Tom Woiwode, Managing Director At Versant Ventures And Chairman Of Seawolf Therapeutics

Remedy Robotics Raises $62 Million Series B to Bring Life-Saving Cardiovascular Intervention to Patients Everywhere
News provided by

Funding will support clinical trials, advancement toward FDA approval, and planned commercial deployment of the company's AI-enabled endovascular robotic platform and software suite
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Remedy Robotics, Inc. ("Remedy"), a leading healthcare and physical AI company developing robotic systems for cardiovascular care and endovascular intervention, today announced it has raised $62 million in Series B funding to accelerate its mission of delivering flawless, immediate robotic care to all patients, regardless of location.
The funding will support several major milestones, including a planned pivotal clinical trial in partnership with the University of California and advancement toward FDA approval for neurovascular intervention. Remedy will also deploy prototype N1 Systems across its network of clinical partners, including through its strategic partnerships with SVIN Mission Thrombectomy and the Australian Stroke Alliance, while continuing to advance the system's industry-leading AI capabilities and autonomous functions.
"Endovascular intervention is the gold standard treatment for stroke and many cardiovascular emergencies, yet access remains limited to a small number of hospitals. For these time-critical conditions, that's devastating. Even when specialist intervention is available, treatment is often delayed, and complications are frustratingly common," said Dr. David Bell, CEO and Co-founder of Remedy Robotics . "This funding will allow us to accelerate toward deployment of our N1 System so we can bring quality intervention to patients everywhere, regardless of geography."
DCVC led the Series B, with participation from new investors including UC Investments (the University of California's investment office), Skip Capital, and Hostplus (one of Australia's largest pension funds). Existing investors Build Collective by Tony Fadell, Blackbird, Divergent Capital and KdT Ventures doubled down.
"Remedy Robotics represents a new generation of medical robotics and physical AI companies, focused not only on technical innovation, but on solving real-world challenges," said James Hardiman, General Partner at DCVC . "We believe the company is uniquely positioned to redefine how life-saving intervention is delivered and are thrilled to support them as they advance toward broader clinical and commercial adoption."
Remedy is finalizing development of the N1 System, an AI-enabled robotic platform and software suite that uses machine learning to analyze preoperative imaging, simulate cases in advance, provide real-time 3D-2D image registration and complete entire endovascular procedures robotically. Designed for on-site, remote, or autonomous operation, the system has the potential to dramatically expand access to and improve the quality of specialized neurovascular, coronary, and peripheral vascular care. Remedy now works with more than 100 hospitals worldwide and is among a small group of physical AI companies bringing robotics into real-world clinical use. In October 2025, Remedy announced that it had successfully completed the world's first remote neurointerventional procedures using the N1 System.
"This funding will allow our world-leading hardware, software, and machine learning teams to progress the N1 system towards clinical trials and potential FDA approval, while also developing additional features including full autonomy," said Jake Sganga, CTO and Co-founder of Remedy Robotics . "We are particularly excited to deepen our partnership with the University of California, having worked closely with their clinical experts since 2021, and as we prepare for our planned pivotal clinical trials to be held across the UC network."
"Remedy is building the kind of company we look for at Blackbird: one with world-class technical talent, a massive global problem to solve, and the potential to create an entirely new category," said Michael Tolo, Partner at Blackbird . "We believe Remedy is uniquely positioned to transform how endovascular care is delivered, and we are excited to support the company through its next phase of growth."
Cardiovascular disease, including stroke and heart attack, is the leading cause of death globally—claiming nearly 20 million lives each year—about twice the toll of all cancers. Beyond the human cost, stroke alone carries an annual economic burden of approximately $891 billion worldwide through healthcare costs and lost productivity. Access to endovascular intervention, the most effective treatment for many cardiovascular conditions, remains severely limited because only highly specialized physicians at a small number of hospitals can perform it. Today, just 2.8 percent of eligible stroke patients worldwide have access to endovascular treatment, leaving millions each year with otherwise preventable disability. Because cardiovascular emergencies are so time-critical, patient outcomes vary sharply based on proximity to specialized care, even in countries with well-developed specialist networks, such as the United States. Remedy's technology directly addresses this access gap, delivering expert care for stroke, severe heart attacks, hemorrhagic conditions, and other time-critical cardiovascular emergencies to patients wherever they are.
Remedy aims to elevate the standard of care across the cardiovascular continuum, from diagnosis to discharge and surveillance, with the goal of making flawless, immediate cardiovascular care available to patients everywhere, from San Francisco to rural areas of Arkansas where timely care is out of reach, or to Lagos, Nigeria, where intervention is almost entirely unavailable.
The N1 System is under development and is not currently available for sale or clinical use in any jurisdiction.

candidates.title: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM
candidates.snippet: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM TechCrunch
candidates.text:
Dreamteam , a startup founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million to challenge Salesforce and HubSpot with its AI-native CRM, betting that AI can finally shake up a market where established players have so far proved difficult to dislodge.
The funding comprises seed and Series A rounds, led by Together Fund and Accel respectively, with participation from Premji Invest. The San Francisco-based startup declined to disclose the size of each round or its valuation.
Traditional CRMs depend on salespeople to manually record customer interactions and keep deal information up to date. That often leaves businesses with incomplete or outdated information. Dreamteam aims to eliminate much of that work by automatically capturing context from sources including emails and customer conversations. It also uses AI agents to handle tasks such as follow-ups, meeting preparation, and pipeline monitoring.
Dreamteam co-founder and CEO Anand Venkatraman (pictured above, right) told TechCrunch that he had repeatedly encountered problems with traditional CRM platforms over more than 25 years in enterprise software, including at Salesforce and Freshworks. Salespeople spent considerable time updating records, yet managers still struggled to get a reliable picture of their business. “In all these years, I have never come across an instance where I could click a button and get a forecast from the CRM,” he said.
That experience led Venkatraman to co-found Dreamteam in 2025 with Senthil Kanthaswamy (pictured above, center), who spent more than nine years at Freshworks, most recently as a product leader at Freshservice, and Ramesh Parthasarathy (pictured above, left), who previously worked on AI and platform engineering at Freshworks.
At the heart of Dreamteam’s CRM is what it calls the Company Brain. This acts as virtual memory, pulling together information from emails, meetings, and other customer interactions to build a shared record of customer relationships. Four built-in AI agents use that information to research prospects, draft follow-up emails, flag potential risks to deals, and configure CRM workflows, with sales teams retaining control over what gets sent to customers.
Dreamteam has signed up more than 100 customers across 13 countries in the three months since it began actively selling its product, with most paying for the service, Venkatraman said. The startup has also replaced established CRM platforms at several businesses, including Salesforce at healthcare company DMS Health and HubSpot at other customers.
The advertising sales team at media streaming company Plex also chose Dreamteam over HubSpot and other AI-native CRM alternatives, Venkatraman told TechCrunch. Plex’s co-founder and chief product officer Scott Olechowski said Dreamteam’s ability to integrate with AI tools already used across the company was a “game changer.”
Replacing established CRM platforms at scale may prove more difficult. In a blog post earlier this year, venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) argued that while AI could transform how businesses manage customer relationships, existing CRMs are likely to remain the systems where customer records are stored, with a new generation of AI-powered tools capturing much of the value by working on top of them.
Venkatraman acknowledged that Salesforce and HubSpot are unlikely to disappear anytime soon, but noted that their entrenched positions do not guarantee they will dominate the next generation of CRM software.
“We see this as an electric-car moment for systems of record,” he said, adding that AI requires a fundamental rethink of how CRMs are built — not simply adding new features to existing platforms.
Kanthaswamy believes startups have a window of two to five years to gain ground before established CRM providers can fully adapt to AI. Rebuilding software around a fundamentally different architecture takes time, he stated, giving newer companies an opportunity to attract customers while incumbents work to overhaul their existing products.
Dreamteam also plans to expand beyond sales into other parts of the customer lifecycle, including onboarding, customer support, and upselling. The startup already has a feature called Magic Apps that allows users to create custom applications and dashboards within the CRM using natural-language instructions, without writing code.
Currently, Dreamteam employs more than 35 people, with its engineering team based in Chennai and its go-to-market operations in the United States. Kanthaswamy said the startup aims to reach eight figures in annual revenue by the end of 2027, though he declined to disclose the startup’s current revenue.

Led by Blue Cloud Ventures, the round brings total funding to $96 million, with more than 1,500 dealerships across the U.S. and Canada already running on Numa's AI Operating System
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Numa , the AI Operating System for dealerships, today announced a $45 million Series C led by Blue Cloud Ventures, with participation from Threshold Ventures, Costanoa, Touring Capital, Gradient Ventures and Tokio Marine Future Fund. The round brings Numa's total funding to $96 million. It caps a year in which Numa tripled in size, tripled its annual recurring revenue and became the AI system GM, FordDirect, BMW and Stellantis each put in front of their dealerships.
Numa has already won the hardest part of the dealership: the customer conversation. The system has handled more than 1 billion calls, texts and chats and booked more than 4 million appointments. Dealerships that run on Numa stay and grow with it. Net revenue retention has risen over the past year, and more dealerships are moving to longer agreements.
For decades, dealership software was built one task at a time. Each system kept its own record of what happened, and none of them acted on what the customer just said. The first wave of AI did not change that. It answered faster, then handed the work back to people to chase by hand.
Numa does not hand the work back. It knows not just who the customer is but what they need, and it acts on it: booking the visit, finding the right car, routing the call or flagging the customer about to leave.
"In two years, every general manager will have an AI COO," said Tasso Roumeliotis, founder and CEO of Numa. "At more than 1,500 dealerships, they already do, and it is Numa. It knows every conversation in the store, sees what needs attention and runs the work that follows. That is not another dashboard or another point tool. It is an operating system. The DMS was built to record the dealership. It was never built to run it. Numa was, and this round puts more engineers to accelerate it."
"What is unique about Numa is that the company understands the DNA and culture of a dealership and seamlessly AI-enables the workflow while empowering all constituents including the dealerships customers", added Mir Arif, Managing Partner of Blue Cloud Ventures. "Numa is not prescriptive but rather deeply understands the objectives of the BDC representative, the salesperson, the service technician, the parts specialist and the sales manager and significantly enhances their productivity."
"As an insurer, we view dealerships as a critical part of the ecosystem that supports customers throughout their vehicle ownership journey," said Mitsutoshi Shizuru, Managing Executive Officer of Tokio Marine & Nichido Fire Insurance Co., Ltd, "Numa is using AI to make this important customer touchpoint faster, more efficient, and more seamless. We believe Numa's technology has the potential to revolutionize the relationship between dealerships and their customers and help shape the next generation of mobility customer experiences in the U.S. and beyond."
This year, Numa took its system across the whole store.
In the service lane, Numa already knows every conversation. In August, Numa acquired SocketTime to put the work behind those conversations into the same system, so what a customer tells the store and what the store does about it run in one place.
In sales, Numa for Sales, launched this month, as the first agent with Inventory Fluency. It knows every new and used vehicle on the lot down to the trim, features and miles, learns each buyer's situation and gets them in the car that fits best, even when the one they called about has sold. Every qualified lead lands in the dealership's CRM with the full conversation, so the salesperson who picks it up already knows the buyer.

It answers first, understands why each customer is calling and puts them in the right hands with that reason carried through. When the phone rings, everyone at the dealership knows the call is for them. Operator continues to climb above 95% with calls going to the right destination.
LiveCSI™ reads customer interactions as they happen and flags the ones putting satisfaction at risk while there is still time to fix them, instead of waiting for a survey to report what went wrong. In 90 days, it analyzed 50 million interactions.
Every dealership on Numa now has over 25+ natural voices to choose from, with regional accents, a new Spanish voice, sharper recognition of vehicle makes, models and VINs, and adjustable speaking speed. The voice on the line sounds like someone who works at the dealership. It comes at no added cost, with nothing for the store to set up.
Three of the largest automakers in North America have each chosen Numa. GM named Numa an iMR Approved Turnkey Vendor, and more than 240 GM dealerships run on Numa today. In those stores, reply times have dropped from 23 hours to 24 minutes, each store saves about $11,000 a month, and 86% of customers flagged as heat cases return for service within six months. FordDirect selected Numa as its strategic AI vendor, making Numa available to more than 3,000 Ford and Lincoln dealerships. Numa is also approved on Stellantis' MarketCenter, opening access to more than 2,600 dealerships in the U.S. and 440 in Canada.

University Of Tennessee: $27 Million Army Research Laboratory Renewal To Advance Military Materials And Manufacturing
By Amit Chowdhry
Yesterday at 5:34 PM
University Of Tennessee: $27 Million Army Research Laboratory Renewal To Advance Military Materials And Manufacturing
The University of Tennessee has secured up to $27 million in renewed sponsorship from the U.S. Department of War’s Army Research Laboratory to advance materials science and manufacturing technologies supporting military applications.
The funding will support the university’s multidisciplinary Defense Development and Applied Research Center (DARC) and multiple departments within the Tickle College of Engineering from 2026 through 2030.
The research focuses on developing advanced materials, improving manufacturing processes, and addressing supply chain challenges affecting military equipment.
New Partnership With Leidos
The renewed sponsorship will support a new research partnership between the university and industrial partner Leidos.
The collaboration will examine equipment assembly timelines and identify supply chain bottlenecks that could be addressed through additive manufacturing.
Researchers will investigate alternative manufacturing approaches that can produce mission-critical components faster or at lower cost while maintaining or improving performance.
The university’s capabilities include developing carbon-based composites, hybrid materials, and ceramic composites designed to withstand demanding operating environments.
Researchers also use advanced imaging and characterization equipment to evaluate complex materials, including additively manufactured components.
Expanding Research Collaboration Across Tennessee
The funding will also expand collaboration with the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga.
Starting in 2026, researchers at UTC’s Nanoengineering Center will contribute theoretical and simulation expertise to complement UT Knoxville’s experimental materials research.
High-fidelity simulations will help researchers understand the mechanisms responsible for material performance and degradation.
AI-assisted predictive models will also help reduce reliance on trial-and-error experimentation.
The collaboration is intended to generate more information from each experiment while accelerating the development of materials for military applications.
Developing Materials For Extreme Environments
Military equipment frequently operates under extreme temperatures, mechanical stresses, and other challenging conditions.
The university is developing lightweight, stable, and fatigue-tolerant composites that combine the strengths of multiple materials.
These technologies could improve the performance and reliability of military components while supporting more efficient manufacturing.
The renewed ARL sponsorship also provides research opportunities for faculty and students across the university system.

Accountable Launches to Give Power to American Taxpayers
News provided by
Accountable
Nov 16, 2026, 09:00 ET
Share this article
